newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's year-to-date U.S. same store sales up.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's year-to-date U.S. same store sales up.

text.p: McDonald's Corp on Tuesday said its year-to-date U.S. same store sales were up compared with a year ago, following more than a year of declines.
Mike Conley, McDonald's chief financial officer, did not specify the amount of the increase.
"Our sales for the first couple of months of the year are going in the direction we'd like to see them go in," Conley said in a telephone interview.
When asked, Conley said U.S. same store sales, looking at January and February to date, show an increase from a year ago.
If the rise in U.S. same-store sales continues through March, McDonald's would post its first positive quarterly comparison in well over a year.
In January, McDonald's said its U.S. same store sales -- measuring results from units open at least a year -- were negative in the fourth quarter and for all of 1996.
The fourth quarter of 1996 was McDonald's sixth consecutive quarter of declines in U.S. same store sales, according to Dean Witter analyst David Adelman.
For January 1997, McDonald's did face an easier comparison since U.S. sales in the previous year were hurt by severe winter weather.
"(January 1996) was their worst month in years," Adelman said.

Conley said McDonald's sales in the year-to-date period benefited from several factors, including its current Chicken McNugget promotion and a January promotion for its french fries. He added that McDonald's remains pleased with the performance of its premium sandwiches.
Asked about McDonald's pricing strategy, Conley declined to give specifics, although he reiterated that the company intends to become more aggressive in offering value to customers.
"We're looking to become more aggressive," Conley said, adding the company is focusing on value. "It (value) can incorporate pricing."
